summary: Closure review: authors addressed several concerns (preregistration, execution accounting, explicit statement that repair was not invoked, Clopper–Pearson bound, and discussion of shared_initial_candidate effects). However, key required revisions from the previous terminal review remain only partially resolved: the manuscript still contains excessive inline provenance/artifact inventories instead of concise scholarly prose; it lacks a concise, standalone technical definition of the forbidden-reachability predicate and a clear, compact summary of each validator's detection assumptions; and the Results/figures remain verbose and provenance-heavy instead of a compact numeric presentation (table/figure) with artifact pointers moved to a short artifact-verification paragraph. These remaining items are resolvable from the supplied evidence bundle and must be fixed before finalisation.
critical_issues: Manuscript remains metadata/provenance-heavy: large inline lists of artifact paths, hashes, and manifest contents appear throughout Methods, Results, and Discussion, harming readability and making the paper read like an artifact inventory rather than a concise short conference paper (previous required revision #2 not fully implemented).

Missing concise technical definition of the core predicate and validators: the manuscript refers repeatedly to a 'forbidden-reachability' predicate and to two deterministic validators (Batfish-style execution validator and a static analyzer) but does not provide a short, precise paragraph that (a) defines the predicate concretely (which reachability pairs/policy semantics are tested; ACL/route-policy/ECMP assumptions) and (b) summarizes each validator's algorithmic/semantic assumptions and failure modes—this was requested as a required revision and remains only partially addressed.

Results presentation is still verbose and interleaved with provenance: although contingency counts, p-value, bootstrap CI, and Clopper–Pearson bound are reported, the Results section includes extensive artifact listings and provenance. The paper should present the principal statistics compactly (one small table or figure plus concise text) and relocate extended artifact-path/hash listings to a short verification paragraph or an explicit archived-manifest citation (previous required revision #5 not fully implemented).
required_revisions: Compress provenance material: remove long inline artifact/path/hash listings from the main narrative. Replace them with concise scholarly prose (one short paragraph) that states where the complete artifact bundle and hash manifest are archived and provide at most a few representative filenames/sha256 values needed for immediate verification. Retain full manifest in the evidence bundle; do not reproduce it inline in Methods/Results/Discussion. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Add a concise technical subsection (≤1 paragraph) in Methods that (a) precisely defines the 'forbidden-reachability' predicate used in scoring (specify the reachability pairs tested, whether ACL/route-policy semantics are included, and the operational meaning of a violation), and (b) summarizes each validator's detection model and limitations (what each validator checks, its execution vs static-analysis assumptions, known false-negative risks). Cite per-episode validator_trace artifacts for full detail. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Condense Results: present the primary numerical outcomes (paired contingency table, McNemar p-value, bootstrap 95% CI, Clopper–Pearson upper bound) as a compact narrative plus one small table or single-panel figure. Move extensive numeric breakdowns, per-task examples, and artifact pointers to one short verification paragraph that points to the archived files (execution/ and analysis/ paths). Ensure the compact presentation appears in the main five pages. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)

Edit Abstract, end-of-Introduction contributions list, and Conclusion to make the primary interpretive limitation front-and-center: explicitly state that the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis about repair efficacy was untestable in this run because (a) shared_initial_candidate semantics replayed the same initial candidate to both arms and (b) no validator-detected baseline violations occurred; state clearly that the empirical contribution is deterministic execution accounting, artifact archiving, and design lessons for follow-up stress tests. (Resolvable from supplied artifacts.)
optional_revisions: Provide a one-paragraph evidence-to-claim mapping (compact) that links each principal manuscript claim to the exact archived artifact(s) (filenames/manifest path and sha256) that substantiate it (can be short; full manifest already supplied).

Add a short paragraph estimating the model-call vs inferential-power trade-off (example: independent two-draw per pair would double model_calls to ~600 under the provided manifest) to help readers plan follow-up experiments; cite execution/model_configuration.json and execution/execution_manifest.json for current accounting.
